sections.text:
By 1982, the American band Survivor had released two unsuccessful albums and were concerned they would be dropped by their record label. That year, the director and actor Sylvester Stallone enlisted them to write a song for his film Rocky III, after Queen denied him permission to use "Another One Bites the Dust". Stallone asked for "something street" with a pulse to match the punches of the boxing scenes. He sent them a copy of the montage used in the film's introduction, depicting the boxer Rocky Balboa and the ascent of his rival, Clubber Lang.

"Eye of the Tiger" was written by the guitarist, Frankie Sullivan and the keyboardist, Jim Peterik. They conceived a riff based on chord changes to mirror the timing of punches. It combines hard rock with a post-disco beat. The title was taken from a line spoken by the Rocky character Apollo Creed: "You had that eye of the tiger, man, the edge ... You gotta get it back." Stallone took the phrase from the 1969 film A Dream of Kings. 

Survivor initially planned to title the song "Survival", and had the chorus: "Rising up to the spirit of our rival / And the last known survivor stalks his prey in the night / And it all comes down to survival", with "survival" rhyming with "rival". They changed it as they felt the "eye of the tiger" hook was stronger and did not have to rhyme perfectly.

Survivor recorded a demo at the Chicago Recording Company on February 1, 1982. Sullivan was so destitute that he used a guitar with a broken headstock he had glued back together. The band attempted to capture a drum sound similar to that of the Led Zeppelin drummer, John Bonham. Stallone loved the demo and insisted on using it in the film. Survivor rerecorded it for the album and single releases.

sections.heading: Release
sections.wikitext:
"Eye of the Tiger" was played extensively on [[MTV]] and radio, and topped charts worldwide during 1982. In the US, it was number one on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for six weeks.<ref name="Grdn" /> In August 1982, it was [[certified platinum|certified double platinum]] in the US for sales of two million copies.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoffman |first=Christopher |date=2022-05-30 |title=Survivor's Frankie Sullivan talks making of 'Eye of the Tiger' on {{as written|i|t's [sic]}} 40th anniversary |url=https://utv44.com/entertainment/survivors-frankie-sullivan-dispels-rumors-about-eye-of-the-tiger-on-it40th-anniversary-rocky-sylvester-stallone-blockbuster-million-platinum |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=[[WJTC]] |language=en}}</ref> "Eye of the Tiger" sold 956,000 copies in the UK and was number one on the [[UK singles chart]] for four weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=Survivor |url=http://www.officialcharts.com/artist/19687/survivor/ |access-date=September 7, 2017 |publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]}}</ref> It was the UK's third-best-selling single in 1982.<ref>{{cite web |last=Copsey |first=Rob |date=March 12, 2021 |title=The Official Top 50 best-selling songs of 1982 |url=https://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/the-official-top-50-best-selling-songs-of-1982__32665/ |access-date=July 10, 2021 |publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]}}</ref> By February 2015, It had sold more than 4.1 million in downloads in the US.<ref name="Digital">{{cite news |last=Grein |first=Paul |date=February 4, 2015 |title=The 15 Most Downloaded Songs in Rock History |publisher=[[Yahoo! Music]] |url=https://music.yahoo.com/photos/top-selling-rock-songs-1422920108-slideshow/survivor-photo-1423002874544.html |url-status=dead |access-date=June 25, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119143803/https://music.yahoo.com/photos/top-selling-rock-songs-1422920108-slideshow/survivor-photo-1423002874544.html |archive-date=January 19, 2016}}</ref> Sullivan felt people related to the message of self-empowerment: "It's about getting your ass out of bed. It's about saying: 'I'm not going to ''try'' to go to the gym Monday – I ''am'' going to go to the gym Monday.'"<ref name="Grdn" />

At the [[25th Annual Grammy Awards]], "Eye of the Tiger" won [[Best Rock Performance by Duo or Group with Vocal]] and was nominated for [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]], but lost to "[[Always on My Mind]]" by [[Willie Nelson]].<ref name="Grammy">{{cite web |title=25th Annual Grammy Awards (1982) |url=https://www.grammy.com/awards/25th-annual-grammy-awards |access-date=February 19, 2021 |website=[[Grammy Award|Grammy.com]]}}</ref> At the [[55th Academy Awards]], it was nominated for [[Academy Award for Best Original Song|Best Original Song]] (the only nomination for ''Rocky III''), but lost to "[[Up Where We Belong]]" from ''[[An Officer and a Gentleman]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=The 55th Academy Awards – 1983 |url=https://www.oscars.org/oscars/ceremonies/1983 |access-date=September 28, 2019 |website=Oscars.org |date=October 5, 2014 |publisher=[[Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences]]}}</ref> The music video depicts the band members walking through city streets and an industrial warehouse. In May 2024, it reached one billion views on [[YouTube]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Gil |date=2024-05-30 |title=Survivor's ''Rocky III'' anthem 'Eye of the Tiger' hits 1 billion views mark on YouTube |url=https://www.billboard.com/music/rock/survivor-eye-of-the-tiger-1-billion-views-youtube-1235696266/ |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Eye of the Tiger" was played extensively on MTV and radio, and topped charts worldwide during 1982. In the US, it was number one on the Billboard Hot 100 chart for six weeks. In August 1982, it was certified double platinum in the US for sales of two million copies. "Eye of the Tiger" sold 956,000 copies in the UK and was number one on the UK singles chart for four weeks. It was the UK's third-best-selling single in 1982. By February 2015, It had sold more than 4.1 million in downloads in the US. Sullivan felt people related to the message of self-empowerment: "It's about getting your ass out of bed. It's about saying: 'I'm not going to try to go to the gym Monday – I am going to go to the gym Monday.'"

At the 25th Annual Grammy Awards, "Eye of the Tiger" won Best Rock Performance by Duo or Group with Vocal and was nominated for Song of the Year, but lost to "Always on My Mind" by Willie Nelson. At the 55th Academy Awards, it was nominated for Best Original Song (the only nomination for Rocky III), but lost to "Up Where We Belong" from An Officer and a Gentleman. The music video depicts the band members walking through city streets and an industrial warehouse. In May 2024, it reached one billion views on YouTube.

sections.text: In 2012, Survivor sued the Republican presidential candidate Newt Gingrich in Illinois federal court for using "Eye of the Tiger" without authorization as entrance music at his political rallies. The lawsuit was settled out of court. In the same year, another Republican candidate, Mitt Romney, agreed to stop using "Eye of the Tiger" at his rallies. In 2016, the Republican candidate Mike Huckabee agreed to pay $25,000 in compensation for using "Eye of the Tiger" at a rally without permission.
